scenario.topic: Decide which accessibility features to prioritize in a campus app

options.name: Voice Navigation and Commands
options.upside: Enables hands-free app navigation for users with visual or mobility challenges.
options.concern: May require quiet environments and can struggle with diverse accents or speech impairments.

options.name: High Contrast and Customizable Text Sizes
options.upside: Improves readability for users with visual impairments and personalizes display settings.
options.concern: Limited benefit for users with cognitive disabilities or those needing alternative input methods.

options.name: Real-Time Captioning and Transcripts
options.upside: Provides immediate text alternatives for audio content, aiding comprehension.
options.concern: Requires stable internet connection and may have occasional transcription inaccuracies.

options.name: Haptic Feedback and Vibration Alerts
options.upside: Offers non-visual notifications and confirmations to improve user awareness.
options.concern: Effectiveness varies by device hardware and may not be noticeable in noisy or busy environments.

shared_context: A campus app is being developed to improve accessibility for all students and staff. The group must prioritize which accessibility features to implement first, considering usability, technical complexity, and impact on diverse user needs.

personas.name: Maya
personas.background: Maya is a student advocate focused on improving campus usability for visually impaired users.
personas.private_goal: Ensure the app is easy to read and accessible for users with low vision.

A.reason_for: Helps visually impaired and mobility restricted users navigate hands-free.
A.reason_against: Medium complexity and may struggle with diverse speech patterns.

B.reason_for: Directly improves readability and customization for low vision users.

C.reason_for: Supports hearing impaired and non-native speakers, broadening accessibility.
C.reason_against: High complexity and requires stable internet.

D.reason_for: Provides tactile feedback that can aid attention and hearing impaired users.

personas.name: Liam
personas.background: Liam is an accessibility researcher passionate about inclusive communication for all users.
personas.private_goal: Prioritize features that enable better comprehension for hearing impaired and non-native speakers.

A.reason_for: Useful for mobility restricted and visually impaired users.
A.reason_against: Speech recognition challenges and environment limitations.

B.reason_against: Does not address audio or speech needs.

C.reason_for: Provides real-time text alternatives critical for hearing impaired users.

D.reason_for: Offers non-visual alerts beneficial for hearing impaired users.
D.reason_against: May be less effective on some devices.

personas.name: Zara
personas.background: Zara is a campus IT support specialist focused on low-complexity, high-impact solutions.
personas.private_goal: Implement features that are easy to deploy and benefit the largest group of users quickly.

A.reason_for: Medium complexity and aids visually impaired users.
A.reason_against: Implementation time is longer and environment dependent.

B.reason_for: Low complexity and quick to implement with broad visual benefits.

C.reason_for: Important for hearing impaired but complex and slow to implement.
C.reason_against: High technical demands and internet reliance.

D.reason_for: Moderate complexity and useful for hearing impaired and attention deficit users.

personas.name: Eli
personas.background: Eli is a faculty member with limited time, focused on straightforward accessibility improvements.
personas.private_goal: Prioritize simple, effective features that require minimal maintenance.

A.reason_for: Useful for some users but requires quiet spaces and more effort to maintain.

B.reason_for: Easy to implement and maintain, benefits many users immediately.

C.reason_for: Valuable for hearing impaired but too complex and resource intensive.
C.reason_against: High implementation time and internet dependency.

D.reason_for: Provides useful alerts with moderate complexity.

personas.name: Nina
personas.background: Nina is a student with hearing impairment advocating for non-visual alert systems.
personas.private_goal: Ensure the app provides effective notifications and confirmations for hearing impaired users.

A.reason_for: Helps visually impaired and mobility restricted users.
A.reason_against: Less relevant for hearing impaired users like herself.

B.reason_for: Improves visual accessibility which can complement other needs.
B.reason_against: Limited direct benefit for hearing impairment.

C.reason_for: Provides captions helpful for hearing impaired users.
C.reason_against: High complexity and requires stable internet.

D.reason_for: Offers tactile alerts that improve awareness without sound.

personas.name: Omar
personas.background: Omar is a non-native English speaking staff member who benefits from clear audio alternatives.
personas.private_goal: Focus on features that improve comprehension for non-native speakers and hearing impaired users.

A.reason_for: Helpful for mobility restricted users but less critical for his needs.
A.reason_against: Speech recognition may struggle with accents like his.

B.reason_against: Does not address audio content directly.

C.reason_for: Real-time captions greatly aid understanding of audio content.

D.reason_for: Non-visual alerts can help maintain attention.

acceptance_reasons.D: Offers non-visual alerts beneficial for hearing impaired users.
